statement: Today is Wednesday. What day of the week will it be 100 days from today?

choices.misconception: I worked out 2 extra days but counted them backwards from Wednesday.
I thought 100 is a round number, so it must be a whole number of weeks and the day would not change.
I counted today as the first of the 100 days, so I ended one day short.
I threw away the 14 whole weeks but then started counting the 2 extra days from Thursday instead of from Wednesday.

hints: What day is it exactly 7 days from today?
The days of the week repeat every 7 days, so whole weeks can be thrown away. Only the days left over after the whole weeks move you on.
100 days is 14 whole weeks, which is 98 days, and 2 days more.

solutions.reliable: 14 weeks is 14 x 7 = 98 days, so 98 days from today is again a Wednesday. Two more days: Thursday, then Friday. The answer is Friday. The transferable idea: in any repeating cycle, only the remainder after the whole cycles matters.

whyOnTest: Remainders and modular cycles: a day-of-the-week question is the remainder after dividing by 7, and the off-by-one counting slip is offered.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
